issues.description: The parameter order of the teleport_s function in the template does not match the specification in the problem statement nor the implementation in the solution. The problem statement specifies teleport_s(circ, data_qubit, injection_qubit, p=0.0), but the template defines teleport_s(circ, injection_qubit, data_qubit, p=0.0). This mismatch can confuse students about which argument corresponds to the data qubit vs. the injection qubit and may lead to incorrect implementations or tests failing.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template stub for teleport_s to use the same parameter order as the problem statement and solution: def teleport_s(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int, p: float = 0.0) -> int:. This ensures consistency between the spec, template, and reference implementation and prevents student confusion.

issues.description: The parameter order and naming for the teleport_s teleportation routine is inconsistent between the problem statement and the template stub. The problem statement and the solution implementation expect the signature (circ, data_qubit, injection_qubit, p=0.0), but the template repository stub declares the parameters in the opposite order (injection_qubit before data_qubit). This mismatch can confuse students when mapping the described API to the provided starter code and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template stub signature match the problem statement and solution: change the template function declaration to def teleport_s(circ: stim.Circuit, data_qubit: int, injection_qubit: int, p: float = 0.0) -> int so the parameter order and names are consistent across all artifacts.
